core_category_candidates.description: Categories evaluated as potential core categories, ordered by decreasing suitability (most central first). All candidates must EXIST in categories_summary.

category_label.description: EXACT category name as it appears in categories_summary.

is_central.description: true if this category acts as a hub: multiple other categories connect to it via documented hypotheses.

has_explanatory_power.description: true if this category explains WHY participants behave as they do, not just WHAT they do.

has_theoretical_grab.description: true if connecting this category to others produces emergent insight or 'aha moments'.

centrality_rationale.description: Qualitative reasoning covering: centrality (hub of relationships?), explanatory power (explains WHY?), frequency with variation (appears across docs with nuance?), and theoretical grab. Cite hypothesis IDs [H1], [H2], etc.

connected_categories.description: Category labels this candidate connects to via hypotheses (from categories_summary).

key_hypothesis_refs.description: Hypothesis references supporting this candidate. Use [H1], [H2], etc. format.

recommendation.description: Which category you recommend as core and why. If multiple strong candidates, explain trade-offs. The researcher (HITL) makes the final choice.

no_suitable_core.description: true if no existing category reaches core category level.

no_suitable_rationale.description: If no_suitable_core=true: what is missing (insufficient connections, low explanatory power, categories too descriptive).
